title: Define success criteria and test cases before improving a prompt
prompt:
Act as a prompt-evaluation planner. Before I spend time improving a prompt, help me set up a way to judge it.

My use case: [DESCRIBE WHAT THE PROMPT IS FOR]
My current first draft prompt: [PASTE DRAFT, OR WRITE 'NONE YET']
Things that matter most to me: [E.g. ACCURACY, TONE, FORMAT, SPEED, COST]

Please produce:
1. Success criteria: 3 to 6 criteria that are specific and checkable (not vague words like 'good' or 'helpful'). For each one, say how I would check it.
2. A test set: 8 to 10 realistic test inputs for my use case, including at least 2 edge cases and 1 input the prompt should refuse or flag. For each input, write what a passing answer must contain.
3. A scoring sheet: a simple table with the test inputs as rows and the criteria as columns, so I can mark pass or fail by hand.
4. A note on which failures are likely to be fixed by changing the prompt, and which might be better solved another way (for example a different model, or changing the surrounding workflow).

If no draft prompt exists, also write a first draft that I can run against the test set. Do not claim any result: you have not run these tests, so only plan them.
example_output_summary: A list of checkable success criteria, a set of test inputs with expected pass conditions, a blank scoring table, and a short note on which problems prompt changes can and cannot fix.
